record.paper_title: Answer to Some Open Problems and Global Bifurcation for an Overdetermined Problem
record.original_question: For the same local bifurcation family s → (w_s, T_s) from Theorem 1.1, determine the type of bifurcation at the critical period T*(n): is it subcritical, critical, or supercritical? Equivalently, determine whether ∂_s T(s)|_{s=0} is negative, zero, or positive.

evidence.quote: Open Problem 2. Is the bifurcation at T∗(n) sub-critical, critical, or super-critical? In other words, ∂s (Ts )|s=0 < 0, ∂s (Ts )|s=0 = 0, or ∂s (Ts )|s=0 > 0?

Theorem 1.2. Under the assumptions of Theorem 1.1, ∂s (T (s))|s=0 = 0. It is known from Theorem 1.2 that the bifurcation at T∗(n) is critical. Consequently, the conclusion of Theorem 1.2 gives an affirmative answer to the above Open Problem 2.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Consider the overdetermined elliptic problem on perturbed cylinders in $\mathbb{R}^{N+1}$ ($N\ge 1$). For a positive number $T>0$ and a small parameter $s$, let
$$\Omega_{s,T,w}=\{(x,t)\in\mathbb{R}^N\times\mathbb{R}:|x|<1+s\cos(2\pi t/T)+s\,w(2\pi t/T)\},$$
where $w$ is a $2\pi$-periodic, even function with zero mean. Seek $(u,\Omega)$ such that
$$-\Delta u=\lambda_n u\ \text{in }\Omega,\qquad u=0\ \text{on }\partial\Omega,\qquad \partial_\nu u=\text{const}\ \text{on }\partial\Omega,$$
where $\lambda_n$ is the $n$-th radial Dirichlet eigenvalue of $-\Delta$ on the unit ball $B_1\subset\mathbb{R}^N$, and $\nu$ is the outward unit normal to $\partial\Omega$.

Suppose that there is a critical period $T^*(n)$ at which a local bifurcation from the trivial branch (the straight cylinder $B_1\times\mathbb{R}$ with the radial eigenfunction associated to $\lambda_n$) occurs, producing a smooth one-parameter family
$$s\longmapsto (w_s,\,T_s),\qquad w_0=0,\ T_0=T^*(n),$$
of nontrivial solutions to the overdetermined problem above (with $w_s$ in a suitable space of even, zero-mean periodic functions). 

Determine the type of bifurcation at $T^*(n)$: namely, decide whether
$$\left.\frac{\partial T_s}{\partial s}\right|_{s=0}<0\ (\text{subcritical}),\quad =0\ (\text{critical}),\quad \text{or}\ >0\ (\text{supercritical}).$$
artifact.status_search_result: The question is resolved: under the stated bifurcation hypotheses, $\partial_s T_s|_{s=0}=0$, so the bifurcation at $T^*(n)$ is critical. This is established as the main theorem (Theorem 1.2) in the work answering the open problem, and is referenced in subsequent literature on bifurcation analysis of overdetermined problems on perturbed cylinders.

status_evidence.snippet: Bifurcation curves (w_s, T_s) with w_0=0 and T_0=T_{i,*} for the overdetermined problem on perturbed cylinders.
status_evidence.claim: Confirms the framework of local bifurcation curves (w_s, T_s) at critical periods T*(n) for the overdetermined problem.

status_evidence.title: A bifurcation analysis on a nonlocal overdetermined problem
status_evidence.snippet: Related bifurcation analysis citing the criticality result ∂_s T_s|_{s=0}=0 for the overdetermined problem on cylinders.
status_evidence.claim: Subsequent literature uses the result that the bifurcation at T*(n) is critical.
